correctness.rationale: After reflection, all coordinatewise nearest sites along the segment are in the endpoint rectangle contained in the diamond. The finite and infinite tessellations therefore give the same positive-length sequence, since the half-integer lines are met only at isolated parameters; no segment runs along one. Distinct crossing times count the traversals, which cannot repeat a cell by convexity. Simultaneity requires the coprime reduced coordinates both odd; in that case the g common times are (2h+1)/(2g), 0≤h<g. Removing endpoint cells yields the claimed count, including both axes. The two endpoint ranks must be highest; summing their probability needs no independence across visibility events. The uncorrected diamond shell has 4m sites, and the exceptional primitive ordered pairs of positive odd coordinates of sum 2k are indexed by reduced residues modulo 2k; the four signs and the factor two in the rank probability give the factor eight. The correction at R=2 is already nonzero. The derivative bound on h(x)=1/[x(x+1)] makes the kth group O(k^-2) after summing g. For 2kg>R the small-k tail adds O(R^-1 sum_(k≤R/2) 1/k), and the large-k tail is O(R^-1); the harmonic baseline has the asserted constant and O(R^-1) remainder. Independent summation with a tail bound certifies the displayed decimal rounding.
